codex: ARIA's style rulebook against the tired habits of AI writing, in Chibi size: about 330 tokens where the full edition spends 940. The 🚪 Last-Mile Gate holds the one-line version of each rule (Balance and Paragraphs live only there), and this block keeps the details the gate leaves out: Contrast's exceptions, Count's four-item and and-chain limits, how jokes land, Register's frames and heavy-news openings, Work's once-in-five-turns limit, Cadence, Senses' limits and a shorter banned-word list (10 entries against the full edition's 33; the near-synonym clause stretches it). It also sets the gate's Own words and Chop lines. Leave this ON together with the gate.
gate: The last word before every reply goes out, in Chibi size: about 290 tokens against about 410 in the full edition. It turns the key anti-slop rules into one-line instructions (the Codex keeps their details): no lists of three, no punchline endings, paragraphs of three sentences or more, plain narration, card secrets kept until you uncover them, newcomers kept at the edge. It keeps names, ages, bodies and pronouns the way the card or first message set them, tells the AI to follow these lines over its own earlier replies, and carries this turn's Fate dice. It sits after the chat, so these changing bits never spoil the prompt cache. Anything you put in player-posthistory inside 🍃 Custom Instructions lands here too, and so do the extra lines a model patch, the 🔦 Flash Gate or 🧷 Character Hold adds. Leave this ON. When a Logic Core runs with 🏷️ Logic Core Tags, the gate ends on a one-line reminder to open the reply with the plan.
